records.region: Virginia, United States; Mountain Run and North Anna through Lake Anna to Pamunkey River and the West Point/Mattaponi–York estuarine junction.
records.candidate_name_role: representative downstream river-system identity; not a uniform hydronym for every selected reach

naming_scope_details.component_scope_limits: The selected route combines Mountain Run, North Anna River, the Lake Anna reservoir passage, and Pamunkey River to the West Point/Mattaponi–York junction setting. Pamunkey River is supported as representative identity only. The upper Mountain Run and North Anna names, the distinct northern Pamunkey Creek reservoir arm, and the Lake Anna waterbody remain separate. records.supported_name_scope: Geographic context only: Rink Isbræ is the mapped outlet-glacier label; Karrat Isfjord names the receiving fjord. Neither is accepted as a natural-river name for FID8856.

completion_scope.selected_lake_or_reservoir_links: No lake or reservoir passage requiring a separate connector identification was identified in the selected route and original national cartographic setting.
completion_scope.material_junctions: The selected single mainstem passes from the broad continental-ice setting into the Rink outlet-glacier/fjord setting. No additional selected branch junction is established by the source; neighboring outlets are kept separate.
completion_scope.scale: Ordinary generalized geographic corridor/component scale. Interior ice-setting correspondence and the outlet/fjord transition are established; exact bank, vertex, glacier-front and mouth-point agreement is neither asserted nor required.

records.region: West Greenland; Inland Ice to Rink Isbræ and the inner Karrat Isfjord terminal setting.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: Original cartography accounts for the whole selected Inland Ice, outlet-glacier and inner-fjord setting. No representative natural-river hydronym is established. A glacier name and a fjord name cannot name the complete modeled river object.
geographic_disambiguation: The selected endpoint is in the inner Rink Isbræ–Karrat Isfjord setting, not the outer coast, Upernavik town, or the more southerly Uummannaq coastal settlement.
The separate glacier/fjord arms north of the selected ending provide coastal orientation only; their proximity does not make them selected tributaries or extend their names onto this mainstem.

The retained southern West Greenland Sheet 2 and the Kangerlussuaq/Søndre Strømfjord–Nuussuaq Sheet 3 are not used as positive coverage evidence for this northern selection. No claim of coverage is inherited merely from a prior Greenland finding.

naming_scope_details.component_scope_limits: The selection combines an unnamed glaciated headward passage, the mapped Snow River, Kenai Lake, upper Kenai River, Skilak Lake and the lower Kenai River to Cook Inlet. Kenai River is supported only as the representative system identity. Glacier and lake surfaces are not renamed as rivers, and Snow River keeps its separate mapped scope. No exact source point, legal naming status, modern glacier front, hydronym-transition vertex or exact marine mouth point is established.

records.region: Melville Peninsula, Nunavut, Canada; Kingora–Sarcpa–Hall Lake–Sarvuq Inlet corridor with unresolved connection to Foster Bay.
records.candidate_name_role: Source-supported river-component identity for the western and middle Kingora corridor only. It is not an established representative identity for the entire selected river/lake/Foster Bay route.
records.material_pending_reason: Actual mapped waterway continuity between northern Sarvuq Inlet and the selected southwestern Foster Bay terminal setting is unresolved. Readable geographic coverage and the retained sea terminal class are insufficient to supply the missing lake-to-coast connector.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The original NLUIS47B and47A maps support the selected western Kingora River corridor, its intervening lakes and Sarcpa Lake passage, the lower river connection into Hall Lake, and the selected lake passage toward Sarvuq Inlet. They do not establish the selected northeastward connection from Sarvuq Inlet to the Foster Bay coast. The maps and marginal prose instead identify a separate southeastern Hall Lake outlet through Ikerasak River to Roche Bay. That alternative outlet cannot replace the selected ending. The full selected route therefore remains source-material pending.
records.completion_scope: The original NLUIS47B and47A maps support the selected western Kingora River corridor, its intervening lakes and Sarcpa Lake passage, the lower river connection into Hall Lake, and the selected lake passage toward Sarvuq Inlet. They do not establish the selected northeastward connection from Sarvuq Inlet to the Foster Bay coast. The maps and marginal prose instead identify a separate southeastern Hall Lake outlet through Ikerasak River to Roche Bay. That alternative outlet cannot replace the selected ending. The full selected route therefore remains source-material pending.
records.supported_name_scope: Bounded observed component candidate; whole selected system still pending.

component_scope_limits: Kingora River is a bounded historical cartographic river label; it is not extended to Sarcpa Lake, Hall Lake, Sarvuq Inlet or the unestablished Foster Bay connector.
Sarcpa Lake and Hall Lake retain separate lake identities, and Sarvuq Inlet names the northeastern inlet of Hall Lake on the source.
The Saniraq River approach to Sarcpa Lake and other lateral/northern tributaries remain separate components, not alternative names for the western selected head.

The southeastern Ikerasak River outlet to Roche Bay is independently mapped and described, but is outside the selected northeastern ending. It is not adopted as a replacement route or whole-feature name.
No current formal registry status, uniform scalar name, exact banks, exact shoreline/mouth vertices, present flow direction throughout, or official total length is claimed.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
